q: If we cut Meta spend by 30% next month, what would happen to our profit?

problems: sign differs from the data (the same figure appears there with the opposite sign): 30%

answer:
By order date for sales/profit; ad spend shown on the P&L (delivery date). For Tilting Heads: cutting Meta ad spend by 30% (₹2,56,513) would likely reduce the current Meta loss, provided sales don’t fall too far.

- Where we are (Sep 2026): Meta P&L ad spend ₹8,55,043; Meta net sales (P&L basis) ₹9,39,860; Meta net profit −₹3,11,157.  
- If spend is cut 30% (₹2,56,513) and sales do not change: savings = ₹2,56,513 → Meta net profit improves to about −₹54,644. New Meta ad spend ≈ ₹5,98,530.  
- If spend is cut 30% (₹2,56,513) and sales fall proportionally (−30%): Meta net profit ≈ −₹2,17,810 (smaller benefit than the no-drop case).  
- Breakeven: sales would have to drop by more than ≈47.2% after the cut for profit to be worse than today.

Worth checking: run a staged test (e.g., 10–30% cuts by campaign) and monitor Meta-attributed net sales and conversion; if sales drop <47.2% the cut should improve profit.
